title: Find and negotiate with an order-shipping warehouse
summary: A hobby founder's agent picked warehouses near likely customers, sent specs, gathered terms and negotiated prices with seven contenders; she signed a contract after three days.
agent_role: The agent found warehouses near customers, sent product specs, collected terms and negotiated pricing. The founder reviewed the choice and signed the contract herself.
outcome: Author reports signing with one of 7 warehouses after a 3-day process, mostly spent waiting for replies.
what_they_did: The poster runs a hobby product project. She had her agent find order-packing and shipping warehouses close to likely customers, to cut delivery time. The agent sent them specs, gathered their terms and negotiated prices. She signed the final contract.
how_it_went: She says the agent compared 7 contenders and she signed a contract the same morning. The whole process took 3 days, mostly waiting on the warehouses.
worth_knowing: Most of the time went to waiting for the warehouses to reply, not to the agent's own work.
prompt: I sell [your product] and need a warehouse to store, pack and ship orders. My customers are mostly in [regions]. Find 5 to 8 order-fulfillment warehouses close to those customers. Draft an email for each with my product specs: [size, weight, monthly order volume]. Show me the drafts and wait for my approval before sending. As replies come in, put each company's terms and prices in a spreadsheet. Suggest counteroffers, but ask me before sending any. Then recommend the best option and explain why.

curation.rationale: A concrete, uncommon small-business task where the agent shortlisted, contacted and negotiated with seven warehouses, but the post gives no tools or setup details.
